tier_reason: NVIDIA/cutlass issue #11 (2018-05-21, one user, GTX 1080, CUDA 9.2 samples path, no flags) shows sgemm_tt 2840.5 GFLOPs (0.069216 ms) against matrixMulCUBLAS 3065.46 GFlop/s (0.064 ms), i.e. CUTLASS about 7 percent slower; a single user run with no methodology is C, and the v3.0.0 README chart (CUDA 12.0; 'Relative Peak Performance of GEMM', bars about 85 to 100 percent) and text claim only parity ('comparable to cuBLAS'), so no source opened shows CUTLASS faster than cuBLAS.

corrections.caveats: Not a faster-than-baseline result: the only measured head-to-head found is slightly slower than cuBLAS, so this entry is kept as a parity claim. The measurement is a single 2018 user post (issue opened and closed on 2018-05-21) on a small problem where launch overhead is large, one run per tool, harness timers differ (profiler versus matrixMulCUBLAS), CUDA 9.2 and an old CUTLASS release, no compiler flags. The issue's CUTLASS dgemm lines used a mismatched shape (m=640, n=480, k=320) and are not comparable. README figure for version 3.0 (opened via the v3.0.0 README, bars read by eye and not printed numbers) shows relative peak performance of roughly 85 to 100 percent per data type and layout on A100, A40, H100 and L40; the README text says 'relative to cuBLAS' but the axis is titled relative peak performance of GEMM, and the current README no longer carries any cuBLAS comparison (it shows percent of theoretical peak on Blackwell and Hopper). The v3.4.0 README figure is CUTLASS 3.1 versus 3.0, not versus cuBLAS. Several NVIDIA libraries, cuBLAS included, build on CUTLASS-style kernels, so parity is expected. A third-party page quoting 235+ TFLOPS for FP16 on H100 was blocked here and not used. The book lead says the book benchmarks its own kernel against cuBLAS, not CUTLASS; no book numbers used. Lead not verified here (arXiv and mirrors blocked; search-result summary only): the Stream-K paper (Osama, Merrill, Cecka et al., PPoPP 2023 poster, arXiv 2301.03598), implemented inside CUTLASS, reports a peak speedup of up to 6.7x over cuBLAS on A100 across 32,824 GEMM shapes, with a much smaller average gain (the summary gives about 1.06x average and 0.68x minimum for FP64) and some shapes slower. The repo's examples/47_ampere_gemm_universal_streamk compares Stream-K only with CUTLASS's own data-parallel GEMM (1.196x on 2048x2048x2048 per the source comment, A100 at locked 1005 MHz clocks), not with cuBLAS.

notes: Record is accurate (numbers, dates, developer quote 'comparable to the kernel launched in the CUDA SDK example', 10.7k stars, BSD-3-Clause, last commit 2026-10-20, current README has no cuBLAS speed comparison); verdict is not-faster because the claim is parity and the measured head-to-head is slower. Notable project (10.7k stars), so per catalog policy it may be kept as a parity entry with this shortcoming. Enrichment lead: the Stream-K paper (CUTLASS-based, peak up to 6.7x over cuBLAS per search summary) could support a shape-specific win if a reachable copy is found.
